en: *אִידָּן m. (אדד, see אוּדְרָא) low-cotton, &c., especially bast twisted for a wick. Shabbat II, 1, explained in Babli (20ᵇ) אחוינא, see אַחְוָונָא 3), in Yerushalmi (4ᶜ) עידניתא.

דָּלַק, דָּלֵיק (Biblical Hebrew)
1) to burn; to be illumined. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 39 saw a castle דּוֹלֶקֶת lighted. Bava Kamma VI, 5 ודָלְקוּ and they caught fire. Yerushalmi Shabbat II, beginning 4ᶜ והיא דְלֵיקָה והולכת that it may continue to burn. Ib.ᵈ דְּלֵיקִין are burning.—Part. pass. דָּלוּק enkindled, burning. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 11 מצאתי אותו דָ׳ (Yalkut ib. 16 דּוֹלֵק) I found it still burning. Midrash Till. to Psalms VII, 14 (reference. to לדלקים ib.) שלבם דָּ׳ עליהם (Yalkut and l. דולק) whose hearts within them are burning (with lust).—Eicha Rabbah to IV, 19 [read:] שהיו דולקין אחריהם מַעֲבִיּוֹת (Kohelet Rabbah to V, 2 שמשליכין דֶּלֶק אחריהם) they (the Romans) sent fire after them from their engines (tormenta), see עָבִית.

—2) to pursue eagerly. Eicha Rabbah l. common gender. דּוֹלְקֵיהֶם של ישראל (Kohelet Rabbah l. common gender. רודפ׳; Midrash Till. l. common gender. שונאין) Israel’s persecutors.

Nifal - נִדְלַק to be burnt, destroyed by fire. Orlah III, 1 יִדָּלֵק; יִּדָּלְקוּ must be burnt. Ib. 2 sq.; and from—Yerushalmi Bava Kamma IV, 5ᶜ top דרכן לִידָּלֵק liable to take fire.

Hifil - הִדְלִיק to kindle, light. Shabbat II, 1 במה מַדְלִיקִין what material may be used for the Sabbath lights? Ib. 7 הַדְלִיקיּ וכ׳ light the lamps. Yerushalmi ib. II, 4ᶜ bottom of page; Yerushalmi Terumot XI, 48ᵇ top באה להַדְלִיק וכ׳ she came to get a light from a priest’s wife; and from—V. הַדְלָקָה.

חוֹסֶן m. (חסן I; compare Biblical Hebrew חָסוֹן)
1) strength. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 30 (reference. to Daniel IV, 27) הח׳ שלי the strength is Mine.

—2) tow, oakum. Shabbat II, 1, explained ib. 20ᵇ ‘flax pounded but not carded’; Yerushalmi ib. II, beginning 4ᶜ

ירָוֹקָה f. (preceding)
1) י׳ שעל פני המים grass upon the water, a sort of sea-weed or moss used for wicks. Shabbat II, 1, explained ib. 20ᵇ אוכמתא דארבא, see אוּכָּם.; Yerushalmi ib. II beginning 4ᶜ, see כִּיתָּן.

—2) jaundice. Ib. XIV, 3 שהן לי׳ they are used as a remedy for jaundice.

כַּלָּךְ m. (see כּוּלְכָא) cissaros-blossoms, a woolly substance, see אַגְבִּין. Kilayim IX, 2, explained Yerushalmi ib. 32ᵃ top אגבין קיסריי. Shabbat II, 1. Ib. 20ᵇ היינו כ׳ this (metaxa) is kallakh. Ib.; Menachot 39ᵇ השיראים והכ׳ וכ׳ (garments of) silk, K. &c. (see סְרִיקִין). Shabbat 27ᵃ. Tosefta ib. IX (X), 3 צמר כ׳ Kallakh wool. Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra V, 11 כולך ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Rabbenu Shimshon to Kelim XXVIII, 8 כלך).
לֶכֶשׁ m. the woolly substance of cedar twigs, used for wicks. Shabbat II, 1 (Arukh לֶגֶשׁ), see דְּרִינוֹן and שׂוּכָּא.

מָדִי, מָדִיִּי m. (preceding) Median. Shabbat II, 1, and e., see נָחוּם. Yoma 11ᵇ שער המ׳ a Median gate (archway). Esther Rabbah to I, 22 לשון מ׳ the Median language; and e.—Fem. מָדִית, מָדִיִּית. Ib. Kelim XXIII, 2, see מְדוֹכָה; and e.—plural מָדִיּוֹת. Esther Rabbah to I, 11. Shabbat VI, 6, see פָּרַף. Yerushalmi ib. XII, 13ᶜ bottom of page; ib. IX, end, 12ᵇ חטים מ׳ Median wheat-grains; and e.

מָה, מַה (Biblical Hebrew)
1) something; anything. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 14; Midrash Tanḥuma Ḥayé 3, see בְּלִימָה.

—2) what? which? Chullin 89ᵃ (play on הא̇מ̇נ̇ם א̇ל̇ם̇, Psalms LVIII, 2) מה א̇ומ̇נ̇תו … כא̇ל̇ם̇ which is the best policy for man in this world? Let him act as if he were mute (keep silence). Bava Metzia 63ᵃ, and e. מה לו הן מה לי דמיהן what are they to me and what their equivalent, i.e. what difference does it make whether the purchased objects or their equivalent be delivered?; Yerushalmi Yoma V, 43ᵃ bottom of page מה ביניהן ומה בין דמיהן. Bava Batra 32ᵇ; 31ᵃ מה (לי) לו לשקר what motive could he have to tell a lie? Ib., and e. מה לי לשקר במקום עדים וכ׳ we do not apply the principle that we believe a defendant because he has no motive to lie, where witnesses are on hand; and see from—מה … אף what …?, even so, i.e. as … so. Gittin 23ᵇ מה אתם … אף וכ׳ as you (Bamidbar XVIII, 28) refers to Israelites, so must your delegate be an Israelite. Shabbat 133ᵇ מה הוא … אף וכ׳ as He is gracious and merciful, so be thou &c.; and from—מה … לא כל שכן, see כָּל.—מה … אינו דין, see דִּין II.—מה ל־ … שכן … תאמר what has this to do with …? In this case …, whereas &c., i.e. it is different with … because &c. Kiddushin 4ᵇ מה ליבמה שכן … תאמר וכ׳ the case of a Y’bamah is different, because she can neither be acquired by means of a document, whereas this (an ordinary woman) &c.; and from—מָה נַפְשְׁךָ (in Babli mostly: מִמָּה נפשך; abbr. ממ"נ) whatever be thy opinion (from whatever opinion thou start), i.e. whichever side you take, at all events. Yerushalmi Berakhot I, 2ᵇ מ׳ נ׳ אם וכ׳ at all events (he has offended); if it was day-time when the first stars (on Friday evening) were visible, it was day-time when the first stars (on Sabbath evening) were visible &c.; Shabbat 35ᵇ חייכ חטאת ממ"נ must bring a sin-offering at all events (whether you consider twilight a part of the day or a part of the night). Ib. 34ᵃ (in Chald. dict.) מה נפשך אי וכ׳ whichever side you take, if twilight is day &c. Eruvin 10ᵃ גדולה … למה לי ממ"נ אי וכ׳ what reason was there for saying ‘large …’? In either case (it is incorrect), if it be to permit the use of the larger court &c. Chullin 29ᵃ ממ"נ אי מחצה וכ׳ in either case (the slaughtering is ritually correct); if you adopt the opinion that an exact half is to be considered as if it were the larger portion &c.; and see from—Ib. 78ᵇ מה אם נפשך, see נֶפֶשׁ.—בַּמֶּה a) wherewith? Bava Batra 10ᵇ במה תרום וכ׳ whereby can the horn of Israel be lifted up? Shabbat II, 1; and from—b) in what case? במה דברים אמורים (abbr. בד"א), see אָמַר I.—לָמָּה wherefore? Berakhot 3ᵃ תחלת … סימנא למה לי what need is there for a sign for the beginning of the first watch? Moʿed Katan 28ᵃ ל׳ נסמכה וכ׳ why is the account of the death of Miriam attached to &c.?; and from—לַמֶּה to what?, whereto? Kiddushin 40ᵇ ל׳ צדיקים נמשלים what are the righteous to be compared to?—ל׳ הדבר דומה, see דָּמָה; and from—V. לָמָה.

—3) (relat.) which, what. Pesachim 88ᵇ מה שקנה עבד וכ׳ whatever the slave acquires belongs to the master. Berakhot I, 1 כל מה שאמרו וכ׳ for whatever act the scholars designated the time ‘up to midnight’ &c.; and see from

נָחוּם (Biblical Hebrew) proper noun of a male person Nahum,
1) N. the prophet. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Naḥ., p. 127ᵇ; and e.

—2) N., name of several Tannaim and Amoraim. Peah II, 6; Nazir 56ᵇ נ׳ הלבלר.—Shabbat II, 1, and from נ׳ המדי.—Taanit 21ᵃ, and from נ׳ איש גם זו, see גִּמְזוֹ.—Yerushalmi Taanit I, 64ᵇ top נ׳; (Yerushalmi Berakhot IX, 14ᵃ top תנחום).—Ib. VIII, 12ᵇ bottom of page, and from נ׳ בי ר׳ סימאי; (Pesachim 104ᵃ; Pirkei Avot Zar. 50ᵃ מנחם בר׳ סימאי;) Yerushalmi Megillah I, 72ᵇ bottom of page, and from נ׳ איש קדש קדשים.—Yerushalmi Beitzah V, 63ᵇ R. N. brother of R. Ila; and e.—V. Friedman (edition) Frankel, Introductio in Talmud Hierosolymitanum. Breslau 1870 (Hebrew), p. 116ᵃ

עַמְרָנִיתָא f. (עַמְרָא) woolly, tufty substance. Shabbat 20ᵇ בע׳ דאית ביה it means the woolly substance in it, see שׂוּכָּא. Ib. (explained אִידָּן, ib. II, 1) ע׳ דביני ביני the woolly bast between (the bark and the wood of the willow); see עִירָנִיתָא

פְּתִילָה f. (preceding article)
1) twisted cord, wick. Shabbat II, 1 פְּתִילַת האידן a bast wick; פ׳ המדבר the wick of the desert, see שִׁבְרָא. Ib. פ׳ הבגד the wick made of rags of a garment. Ib. 5 חוץ מן הפ׳ except when he has the intention of saving the wick; and from—plural פְּתִילוֹת. Ib. 20ᵇ עד כאן פסול פ׳ so far the Mishnah refers to wicks unfit for use on the Sabbath. Ib. 21ᵇ; and from—Gittin 58ᵃ שתי פ׳ בנר אחד two wicks in one lamp (euphem. for adultery).

—2) string; bar. Sanhedrin VII, 2 ומדליק את הפ׳ וכ׳ and (the executioner) lights (heats) the string and throws it into his mouth; explained ib. 52ᵃ פ׳ של אבר, see אֲבָר; Yerushalmi ib. VII, 24ᵇ bottom of page פ׳ של בעץ a bar of plumbum album; (oth. opinion) פ׳ של נפט a wick dipped in naphtha. Yevamot 6ᵇ בישול פ׳ boiling (melting) a bar of lead; Shabbat 106ᵃ. Nedarim 49ᵇ שהן דומין לפ׳ של אבר (not לפתילתא) which burn in the stomach like a molten bar of lead.

קִיק I m. (reduplic. of קא; compare קָאַת) name of a bird, pelican. Chullin 63ᵃ קאת זה הק׳ Manuscript Munich (ed. הקוק, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note), the Biblical ḳaath is the modern ḳiḳ, see קָאַת; Yalkut Vayikra 537 הקוק; Yerushalmi Shabbat II, beginning 4ᶜ. Ib. (reference. to שמן קיק Mishnah ib. II, 1) עוף הוא ושמו ק׳ it is a bird whose name is ḳiḳ. [For other opinions on the meaning of שמן ק׳, see קָאוָא, קִיסוֹסָא, קִיקָיוֹן.]

קִיקָיוֹן m. (Biblical Hebrew) ricinus-tree, or the shrub bearing the castor-berry (Greek κίκι, see Smith, Dictionary of Greek and Roman Antiquities, Third American Edition, New-York 1858 section (Parashah) see Cici, and Löw, Löw, Aramäische Pflanzennamen, Leipzig 1881, p. 353 sq.). Shabbat 21ᵃ (explained שמן קיק, Mishnah ib. II, 1) ר"ל אמר ק׳ דיונה Resh Laḳish says, it means oil from Jonah’s Ḳiḳayon. Ib. לדידי … ק׳ דיונה וכ׳ I was shown Jonah’s Ḳ., it resembled &c., see צְלוּלִיבָא
קִירוּתָא f. (denominative of קִירָא) a mass of wax into which a wick is stuck. Shabbat 20ᵇ (explained שעוה, Mishnah ib. II, 1).

שֶׁמֶן m. (Biblical Hebrew; preceding wds.) oil, fat. Shabbat II, 1 ש׳ שרפה oil of T’rumah which is condemned to be burnt on account of contamination; ש׳ קיק, see קִיק. Ib. 2 ש׳ דגים fish-oil; ש׳ אגוזים nut-oil &c. Ib. 17ᵇ שׁמְנָן their oil, manufactured by gentiles; Pirkei Avot Zar. 36ᵃ. Ib. ש׳ רב יהודה וכ׳ as to gentiles’ oil, R. Judah and his court voted on it and permitted it. Pesachim 83ᵇ; Chullin 91ᵃ; 92ᵇ שַׁמְנוֹ the fat surrounding the nervus ischiadicus, see שׁוּמָן; and from—עֵץ ש׳ pine-wood, see עֵץ.—plural שְׁמָנִים, שְׁמָנִין. Shabbat II, 2 מתירין בכל הש׳ allow all kinds of oil to be used for Sabbath lights. Ib. 26ᵃ כל הש׳ יפין וכ׳ all oils are good for ink, but olive oil is the best. Yerushalmi Bikkurim I, 64ᵇ top; and from

שַׁעֲוָה f. (שעי = שׁוּעַ) wax. Shabbat II, 1 ולא בש׳ nor must you use wax in place of oil for the Sabbath light, see קִירוּתָא. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 44 היה לבו רפה כש׳, see שׁוּעַ I. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 91, end (explained נכאת, Breishit XLIII, 11) ש׳ (perhaps a gum, see preceding). Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 35 כש׳ הנתונה וכ׳ like wax that is put on the writing tablet; and from

שׂוּכָּא m. (שכך, see סכך) prickly bark. Shabbat 20ᵇ (explained לכש, ib. II, 1) ש׳ דארזא the bark of a cedar tree. Ib. ש׳ דארזא עץ וכ׳ but the bark of cedar is mere wood (and cannot be used as a wick)! Answ. בעמרניתא וכ׳, see עַמְרָנִיתָא.—V. שַׂוְוכָּא.

We learned in the mishna that one may not light with burnt oil on Shabbat. The Gemara asks: What is burnt oil? Rabba said: It is oil of teruma that became ritually impure. And why did they call it burnt oil? Because its burning is imminent, as it is prohibited to eat this oil and one is obligated to burn it. The Gemara asks: And what is the reason that one may not light with it on Shabbat? The Gemara explains: Because it is a mitzva to burn it, the Sages issued a decree lest, in doing so, he come to adjust the wick in order to hasten its burning. Abaye said to him: But if what you say is so, that the reason for the prohibition is a concern lest he adjust it, then, on a Festival, when adjusting a wick is permitted, it should be permitted to light with burnt oil. Why then did we learn in the mishna: One may not light with burnt oil even on a Festival? The Gemara answers: It is a decree issued by the Sages prohibiting burning it even on a Festival, due to the prohibition to burn it on Shabbat.

Rav Ḥisda said: The reason for the prohibition against lighting a Shabbat lamp with burnt oil is different, as we are not concerned lest one come to adjust the wick. Rather, here, in our mishna, we are dealing with a Festival that fell on Shabbat eve, in which case he must kindle Shabbat lights on the Festival. One may not light a Shabbat lamp with burnt oil on a Festival because one may not burn consecrated items on a Festival, a prohibition that applies to teruma as well. The Gemara asks: But from the fact that we learned in the latter clause, i.e., the next mishna, that one may not light with burnt oil on a Festival, by inference, in the first clause of the mishna we are not dealing with a Festival but rather with a standard Shabbat. Rabbi Ḥanina from Sura said: This mishna must be understood in the following manner: These are not two distinct halakhot; rather, this mishna was stated employing the didactic style of what is the reason. What is the reason that one may not light with burnt oil on a Festival or on a Festival that falls on Shabbat eve? It is because one may not burn consecrated items on a Festival at all.

It was taught in a baraita in accordance with the opinion of Rav Ḥisda. All of these oils with which the Sages said that one may not light on Shabbat, one may light with them on a Festival, with the exception of burnt oil, because one may not burn consecrated items on a Festival.
he: וְלֹא בְּשֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵיפָה וְכוּ׳: מַאי שֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵיפָה? אָמַר רַבָּה: שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁנִּטְמְאָה. וְאַמַּאי קָרוּ לֵהּ ״שֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵיפָה״? — הוֹאִיל וְלִשְׂרֵיפָה עוֹמֵד. וּבְשַׁבָּת מַאי טַעְמָא לָא? מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁמִּצְוָה עָלָיו לְבַעֲרוֹ, גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא יַטֶּה. אָמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, בְּיוֹם טוֹב לִישְׁתְּרֵי! אַלְּמָה תְּנַן: אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בְּשֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵיפָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב? — גְּזֵרָה יוֹם טוֹב אַטּוּ שַׁבָּת.

רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: לְשֶׁמָּא יַטֶּה לָא חָיְישִׁינַן, אֶלָּא הָכָא בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת עָסְקִינַן — לְפִי שֶׁאֵין שׂוֹרְפִין קׇדָשִׁים בְּיוֹם טוֹב. וְהָא מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בְּשֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵיפָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב, מִכְּלָל דְּרֵישָׁא לָאו בְּיוֹם טוֹב עָסְקִינַן! אָמַר רַב חֲנִינָא מִסּוּרָא: ״מַה טַּעַם״ קָאָמַר: מַה טַּעַם אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בְּשֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵיפָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב — לְפִי שֶׁאֵין שׂוֹרְפִין קׇדָשִׁים בְּיוֹם טוֹב.

תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא. כׇּל אֵלּוּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בָּהֶן בְּשַׁבָּת, מַדְלִיקִין בָּהֶן בְּיוֹם טוֹב, חוּץ מִשֶּׁמֶן שְׂרֵיפָה — לְפִי שֶׁאֵין שׂוֹרְפִין קׇדָשִׁים בְּיוֹם טוֹב.

comments.he: המשפט של רבן גמליאל מופיע בסדרה של פירושים למשנת כלאים, אך גם ברשימה אחרת של חומרים שבהם מותר להדליק פתילות בשבת (שבת פ"ב מ"א). בשתי הרשימות מופיע הכלך, בתוך רשימה ארוכה, ובתלמוד מובא מילון זיהויים שלתוכו שורבבה מימרתו המפרשת של רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. וזו לשון הירושלמי: ".. אנבין קיסריי. אמר רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, חיזרתי על כל מפרשי ימים ואמרו לי כולכא שמו. ולא בפתילת האידן – עירניתא, ולא בפתילת המדבר – כשמועה, ולא בירוקה שעל פני המים – כיתן דמיי, ולא בזפת ולא בשעוה" (שבת פ"ב ה"א, ד ע"ג). את המילים "פתילת המדבר" לא חשב המחבר שראוי לפרש ופירשה "כשמועה", כלומר כולם מכירים ויודעים מהו צמח זה. גם את הזפת והשעווה הוא לא תרגם. עצם הצורך לומר "כשמועה" מוכיח שהעורך סבור שמבחינת הז'אנר הספרותי עליו לתרגם את כל המילים, גם אלו שאין לגביהן קושי, והוא מסביר שנמנע מלתרגם כי אין צורך פרשני בכך.

sections.en:
This mishna cites a list of fuels and wicks that one may not use in kindling the Shabbat lights, either because their use might induce one to perform a prohibited labor on Shabbat or because they are not in keeping with the deference due Shabbat. The mishna begins by listing the materials that one may not use as wicks. That is followed by a list of the substances that one may not use as fuel.

With what may one light the Shabbat lamp, and with what may one not light it? With regard to types of prohibited wicks, one may light neither with cedar bast [lekhesh], nor with uncombed flax [ḥosen], nor with raw silk [kalakh], nor with willow bast [petilat ha’idan], nor with desert weed [petilat hamidbar], nor with green moss that is on the surface of the water. With regard to types of prohibited oils, one may light neither with pitch [zefet], nor with wax [sha’ava], nor with castor oil [shemen kik], nor with burnt oil [shemen sereifa], nor with fat from a sheep’s tail [alya], nor with tallow [ḥelev]. Naḥum the Mede says: One may light with boiled tallow. And the Rabbis say: Both tallow that was boiled and tallow that was not boiled, one may not light with them.
sections.he: בַּמֶּה מַדְלִיקִין וּבַמָּה אֵין מַדְלִיקִין. אֵין מַדְלִיקִין לֹא בְלֶכֶשׁ, וְלֹא בְחֹסֶן, וְלֹא בְכָלָךְ, וְלֹא בִפְתִילַת הָאִידָן, וְלֹא בִפְתִילַת הַמִּדְבָּר, וְלֹא בִירוֹקָה שֶׁעַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם. וְלֹא בְזֶפֶת, וְלֹא בְשַׁעֲוָה, וְלֹא בְשֶׁמֶן קִיק, וְלֹא בְשֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵפָה, וְלֹא בְאַלְיָה, וְלֹא בְחֵלֶב. נַחוּם הַמָּדִי אוֹמֵר, מַדְלִיקִין בְּחֵלֶב מְבֻשָּׁל. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֶחָד מְבֻשָּׁל וְאֶחָד שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְבֻשָּׁל, אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בּוֹ:

en: נֵפְטְ m. (probably a transpos. of נטף, a readaptation of νάφθα) naphtha. Shabbat II, 2. Ib. 26ᵃ אין מדליקין בנ׳ לבן וכ׳ white naphtha must not be used for lighting … because it is explosive. Ib. ומה יעשו … אלא נ׳ and what shall the Cappadocians do who have … only naphtha? Yoma 38ᵇ, sq. Yerushalmi Sanhedrin VII, 24ᵇ bottom of page (see שְׂרֵפָה) בפתילה של נ׳ the Mishnah, describing capital punishment by burning, means a wick saturated with naphtha. Yerushalmi Sotah VII, beginning 22ᵇ אש כנגד נ׳ שלהן ‘fire’ (Psalms XVIII, 13) corresponds to the arrows of the human armies tipped in naphtha; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 17 רמה בהן נ׳ he (the besieger) throws naphtha &c. (βέλη πυροφόρα or πυροβόλα).

נָתַר I (Biblical Hebrew; compare נתק) to sever, loosen.

Nifal - נִיתַּר, נִיתּוֹר
1) to be torn loose, be released. Yerushalmi Taanit II, 65ᵈ top, see נָטַשׁ II and נָתשׁ.—Transferred to be untied, released from an obligation; to become permitted. Yerushalmi Yevamot IV, 6ᵇ bottom of page (reference. to Devarim XXV, 10) בית שהוא נִיתָּר וכ׳ a house (of several wives) which is released (from the leviratical marriage) by means of one ḥălitsah (performed on one of the wives). Yerushalmi Bikkurim I, 64ᵇ top כל הביכורים שנראו לִיתּוֹר … אינן נִיתּוֹרִין וכ׳ all the first fruits which are to be released (become permitted by being brought to the Temple) in the land (of Palestine), can become so only by reciting the confession (Devarim XXVI, 5—10). Eruvin 10ᵃ; 12ᵃ חצר נִיתֶּרֶת וכ׳ a court becomes permitted (for Sabbath purposes) by &c., see פַּס. Ib. שהוא נִיתָּר וכ׳ that it is made available &c.; and e.

Hifil - הִתִּיר
1) to loosen, untie, unscrew. Tosefta Shabbat XVI (XVII), 5 שהִתִּירוֹ which one unscrewed; Shabbat XX, 5 מַתִּירִין, see מַכְבֵּשׁ. Ib. 22ᵃ מתירין (ציצית) מבגד לבגד you may untie show-fringes from one garment (and put them) on another garment. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 5 מַתִּירָן ומוציא וכ׳ he unties them (opens the bags) and lets the air in them escape; and from—[Tosefta Sheviit I, 7, see וָתַר.]

—2) to permit, declare permitted, opposed אָסַר. Shabbat 4ᵃ הִתִּירוּ לו וכ׳ would they (the scholars) permit him to take it out &c.? Ib. II, 4 ור׳ יהודה מַתִּיר but R. Judah declares it permitted. Ib. 2 וחכמים מַתִּירִין; and see from—V. מַתִּיר.

—3) to free, surrender; to outlaw, proscribe. Sanhedrin 40ᵇ ה׳ עצמו למיתה did he surrender himself to death?, i.e. did he declare that he would commit the act in spite of the warning which defined it to be a deadly crime? Ib. 41ᵃ (reference. to Devarim XVII, 6) עד שיַתִּיר וכ׳ until he declares himself ready to undergo capital punishment for his act. Chullin 41ᵃ. Yerushalmi Peah I, 16ᵃ עילא … להַתִּיר דמן וכ׳ they wanted a pretext to outlaw the rebels; and from

Hof. - הוּתָּר
1) to be loosened, untied. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 28, beginning, and from הוּתְּרָה הרצועה, see רְצוּעָה. Shabbat XX, 5 אם היה מוּתָּר וכ׳ if it (the clothes press) was (partly) unscrewed on the eve of the Sabbath, he may unscrew it entirely. Bava Kamma 9ᵇ שור מותר an ox that is not tied, opposed קשור. Eruvin II, 1 קשורות אבל לא מוּתָּרוֹת closely tied together, but not tied in a loose way; and e.

—2) to be permitted. Yerushalmi Shabbat II, 5ᵇ bottom of page ה׳ הנדר, see נֶדֶר; Sanhedrin 68ᵃ. Chullin 17ᵃ בתחילה ה׳ להן וכ׳ originally they were permitted to eat the flesh of an animal killed by stabbing (see נְחִירָה). Ib. 9ᵃ נשחטה הותרה when the animal has been slaughtered according to the ritual, it is (absolutely) permitted. Eruvin 93ᵇ שבת כיון שהותרה הותרה as regards Sabbath laws what has been permitted at the entrance of the Sabbath remains permitted the entire day; ib. 70ᵇ כל שה׳ למקצת וכ׳ whatever is permitted for one part of the Sabbath &c.; and see from—Part. מוּתָּר; f. מוּתֶּרֶת; plural מוּתָּרִים, מוּתָּרִין; מוּתָּרוֹת (it is, they are) permitted (of things and persons). Terumot X, 7. Yevamot I, 2 צרתה מ׳ her rival is permitted (to him as wife). Ib. III, 2 ומ׳ באחותה and he is permitted to marry her sister. Ib. II, 10 מותרות לינשא להן may be married to them; and see from—Pesachim 48ᵃ, and e. (reference. to ממשקה ישראל, Ezekiel XLV, 15) מן המותר לישראל of what an Israelite is permitted to drink. Shabbat 108ᵃ (reference. to בפיך, Shemot XIII, 9) מדבר המותר בפיך the Torah must be written on the skin of an animal which is permitted in thy mouth (a clean animal).

עִטְרָן, עִי׳ m. (compare עֲטַר III, and Samaritan איטרן, Breishit XXXVII, 25 for h. לֹט) ʿiṭran, a sort of resin used for lighting in place of oil. Shabbat II, 2 (24ᵇ). Shabbat 26ᵃ; Tosefta ib. II, 4. Yerushalmi ib. II, 4ᵈ ע׳ בין כבה בין דלק וכ׳ ʿiṭran smells badly whether extinguished or burning.
פַּקּוּעָה f. , plural פַּקּוּעוֹת (Biblical Hebrew Coloquintida, Bitter-Apple, a gourd. Shabbat II, 2 שמן פ׳ gourd-oil. Kelim XVII, 17 של פ׳ (שפופרת) the hollow stem of &c.

צְנוֹן m. (see צָנַן) (full grown, round) radish. Berakhot 36ᵃ; Eruvin 28ᵇ, see פּוּגְלָא. Berakhot 57ᵇ. Pirkei Avot Zar. 11ᵃ צ׳ מחתך אוכל radishes cut (digest) the food. Kilayim I, 5 (different interpretation or differently interpreted from נפוץ). Makhshirin IV, 6 צ׳ שבמערה radishes that grow in the water of a cavern; and from—plural צְנוֹנוֹת. Shabbat II, 2 שמן צ׳ radish-oil. Tosefta ib. II, 3 מה יעשו … אלא שמן צ׳ בלבד what shall the Alexandrians do who have only radish oil (for their lamps)? Kilayim I, 9; Yerushalmi ib. 27ᵇ; and e.

שֶׁמֶן m. (Biblical Hebrew; preceding wds.) oil, fat. Shabbat II, 1 ש׳ שרפה oil of T’rumah which is condemned to be burnt on account of contamination; ש׳ קיק, see קִיק. Ib. 2 ש׳ דגים fish-oil; ש׳ אגוזים nut-oil &c. Ib. 17ᵇ שׁמְנָן their oil, manufactured by gentiles; Pirkei Avot Zar. 36ᵃ. Ib. ש׳ רב יהודה וכ׳ as to gentiles’ oil, R. Judah and his court voted on it and permitted it. Pesachim 83ᵇ; Chullin 91ᵃ; 92ᵇ שַׁמְנוֹ the fat surrounding the nervus ischiadicus, see שׁוּמָן; and from—עֵץ ש׳ pine-wood, see עֵץ.—plural שְׁמָנִים, שְׁמָנִין. Shabbat II, 2 מתירין בכל הש׳ allow all kinds of oil to be used for Sabbath lights. Ib. 26ᵃ כל הש׳ יפין וכ׳ all oils are good for ink, but olive oil is the best. Yerushalmi Bikkurim I, 64ᵇ top; and from

שׁוּמְשׁוּם m. (probably from שֶׁמֶשׁ) [sun-flower,] sesamum, sesame (Assyr. šamaššamu). T’bul Yom I, 5 ed. Dehr. (ed. שֻׁמְשׁוּם). Rosh Hashanah 13ᵃ; Menachot 103ᵇ כביצה חסר ש׳ the size of an egg less that of a sesame seed. Ib. 16ᵇ הקטיר ש׳ לאכול ש׳ if he burnt (the handful of the offering), the size of a sesame grain at a time, or with the intention to eat (the remainder), a sesame grain at a time; and e.—Mostly plural שׁוּמְשְׁמִים, שׁוּמְשְׁמִין. Sheviit II, 7. Hallah I, 4. Mekhilta Bo, section (Parashah) 8. Sifré Bamidbar 146. Shabbat II, 2 שמן ש׳ sesame oil (used in lamps). Tosefta ib. II, 3 מה יעשו … שמן ש׳ what shall the Babylonians do who have nothing but sesame oil? Yerushalmi Yoma II, 39ᶜ top אפי׳ ש׳ even as much (of the incense) as the size of a sesame seed.

The Gemara proceeds to discuss the matter of the Tosefta itself, the case of lighting with sap from balsam trees on Shabbat. Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: One may not light with tzori on Shabbat. And Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar would also say: Tzori, which is one of the component spices of the incense in the Temple, is merely the sap that emerges from balsam trees, and is not part of the balsam tree itself. Rabbi Yishmael says: Anything that originates from the tree, one may not light with it; only materials that do not come from trees may be used. Rabbi Yishmael ben Beroka says: One may only light with a substance that emerges from the fruit. Rabbi Tarfon says: One may only light with olive oil alone.

The Gemara relates: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri stood on his feet and, contrary to this statement, said: And what shall the people of Babylonia, who have only sesame oil, do? And what shall the people of Media, who have only nut oil, do? And what shall the people of Alexandria, who have only radish oil, do? And what shall the people of Cappadocia, who have neither this nor that but only naphtha, do? Rather, you have a prohibition only with regard to those substances with regard to which the Sages said: One may not light with them. All other oils are permitted.

And one may light with fish oil and tar. Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says: One may light with gourd oil and naphtha. Sumakhos says: Among the substances that emerge from the flesh of living beings, one may light only with fish oil. The Gemara asks: The opinion of Sumakhos is identical to the opinion of the first tanna, who also permits lighting with fish oil. The Gemara answers: There is a practical difference between them with regard to what Rav Beruna said that Rav said: One is permitted to use molten fat to which oil was added for lighting. They disagree with regard to this halakha; however, their opinions are not defined and it is unclear which of them permits using it and which prohibits using it.
he: גּוּפָא. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בִּצְרִי, וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: צֳרִי אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא שְׂרָף מֵעֲצֵי הַקְּטָף. רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הָעֵץ אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בּוֹ. רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין מַדְלִיקִין אֶלָּא בַּיּוֹצֵא מִן הַפְּרִי. רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֵין מַדְלִיקִין אֶלָּא בְּשֶׁמֶן זַיִת בִּלְבַד.

עָמַד רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי עַל רַגְלָיו וְאָמַר: מַה יַּעֲשׂוּ אַנְשֵׁי בָבֶל שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אֶלָּא שֶׁמֶן שׁוּמְשְׁמִין? וּמַה יַּעֲשׂוּ אַנְשֵׁי מָדַי שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אֶלָּא שֶׁמֶן אֱגוֹזִים? וּמַה יַּעֲשׂוּ אַנְשֵׁי אֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִיָּא שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אֶלָּא שֶׁמֶן צְנוֹנוֹת? וּמַה יַּעֲשׂוּ אַנְשֵׁי קַפּוֹטְקִיָּא שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם לֹא כָּךְ וְלֹא כָּךְ, אֶלָּא נֵפְטְ? — אֶלָּא אֵין לְךָ אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים אֵין מַדְלִיקִין.

וּמַדְלִיקִין בְּשֶׁמֶן דָּגִים וּבְעִטְרָן. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי אוֹמֵר: מַדְלִיקִין בְּשֶׁמֶן פַּקּוּעוֹת וּבְנֵפְטְ. סוֹמְכוֹס אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַבָּשָׂר אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בּוֹ, אֶלָּא בְּשֶׁמֶן דָּגִים. סוֹמְכוֹס הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא? אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּרַב בְּרוֹנָא אָמַר רַב, וְלָא מְסַיְּימִי.

comments.en: ...Rabbi Tarfon says, one may light only with olive oil. Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri stood on his feet, and said: And what shall the people of Babylonia, who have only sesame oil, do? And what shall the people of Medea, who have only nut oil, do? And what shall the people of Alexandria, who have only radish oil, do? And what shall the people of Cappadocia, who have neither this nor that but only naphtha, do?...
comments.he: רשב"א אומר אין מדליקין בצרי ר' ישמעאל אומר כל היוצא מן העץ אין מדליקין בו ר' ישמעאל [בר"י] בן ברוקה אומר אין מדליקין אלא ביוצא מן הפרי ר"ט אומר אין מדליקין אלא בשמן זית בלבד עמד ר' יוחנן בן נורי על רגליו ואמר מה יעשו אנשי בבל שאין להם אלא שמן שומשמין מה יעשו אנשי מדי שאין להם אלא שמן אגוזים מה יעשו אנשי אלכסנדריא שאין להם אלא שמן צנונות מה יעשו אנשי קפוטקיא שאין להם לא זה ולא זה אין לך אלא מה שאמרו [מדליקין בשמן פקועות ובנפט ר"ש שזורי אומר מדליקין בשמן דגים ובעטרן] סומכוס אומר כל היוצא מן הבשר אין מדליקין בו חוץ משמן דגים ר"ש בן אלעזר אומר כל היוצא מן העץ אין בו משום שלש על שלש ומסככין בו חוץ מן הפשתן.

ר' שמעון בן לעזר אומ' אין מדליקין בצרי. ר' ישמעאל או' כל היוצא מן העץ אין מדליקין בו. ר' ישמעאל בי ר' יוחנן בן ברוקה או' אין מדליקין אלא ביוצא מן הפרי. ר' טרפון אומ' אין מדליקין אלא בשמן זית בלבד. עמד ר' יוחנן בן נורי על רגליו ואמ', מה יעשו אנשי בבל שאין להן אלא שמן שמשמין, מה יעשו אנשי מדי שאין להם אלא שמן אגוזים בלבד, מה יעשו אנשי אלכסנדריא שאין להם אלא שמן צנונות, מה יעשו אנשי קפוטקיא שאין להם לא זה ולא זה, אין לך אלא מה שאמרו.

מדליקין בשמן פקועות ובנפט. ר' שמעון שיזורי או' מדליקין בשמן דגים ובעטרן. סומכוס אומ' כל היוצא מן הבשר אין מדליקין בו, חוץ משמן דגין. ר' שמעון בן לעזר אומ' כל היוצא מן העץ אין בו משום שלש על שלש, ומסככין בו, חוץ מן הפשתן. כרך דבר שמדליקין על גבי דבר שאין מדליקין, אין מדליקין בו. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל או' של בית אבה היו כורכין פתילה על גבי אגוז ומדליקין בה.

sections.en: In continuation of the previous mishna, this mishna adds that one may not light with burnt oil on a Festival, as the Gemara will explain below. With regard to lighting Shabbat lamps, there were Sages who prohibited the use of specific oils. Rabbi Yishmael says that one may not light with tar [itran] in deference to Shabbat because tar smells bad and disturbs those in the house. And the Rabbis permit lighting with all oils for lamps as long as they burn properly; with sesame oil, with nut oil, with turnip oil, with fish oil, with gourd oil, with tar, and even with naphtha [neft]. Rabbi Tarfon says: One may light only with olive oil in deference to Shabbat, as it is the choicest and most pleasant of the oils.
sections.he: אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בְּשֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵפָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב. רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בְּעִטְרָן, מִפְּנֵי כְבוֹד הַשַּׁבָּת. וַחֲכָמִים מַתִּירִין בְּכָל הַשְּׁמָנִים, בְּשֶׁמֶן שֻׁמְשְׁמִין, בְּשֶׁמֶן אֱגוֹזִים, בְּשֶׁמֶן צְנוֹנוֹת, בְּשֶׁמֶן דָּגִים, בְּשֶׁמֶן פַּקּוּעוֹת, בְּעִטְרָן וּבְנֵפְט. רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר, אֵין מַדְלִיקִין אֶלָּא בְשֶׁמֶן זַיִת בִּלְבָד:

comments.he: זבחי - אמר רבי משה הכהן: הבהבי - כדברי רז"ל: ולא הבהבה. ויפת אמר: מגזרת הבהב והיו"ד נוסף כמו שדי. והוא הנכון.

en:
הִבְהֵב I (Pilp. of הבב toglow; compare הבל)
1) to singe, parch. Yerushalmi Ma'asrot IV, beginning, 51ᵃ המְהַבְהֵב שיבולין באור if one parches ears over the fire; Tosefta ib. III, 1 המה׳ בשדה וכ׳ (subaudi שיבולין). Menachot X, 4 (66ᵃ). Beitzah 34ᵃ. Shabbat II, 3 ולא הִבְהֲבָהּ and did not singe it (to prepare it for a wick).—Sanhedrin 37ᵃ is it possible for fire to be in contact with flax ואינה מְהַבְהֶבֶת and not to singe?—Part. pass. מְהוּבְהָב lightly roasted. Yerushalmi ib. VIII, beginning, 26ᵃ

—2) to be like coals giving heat without flame; to nod consent without showing anxiety. Berakhot 34ᵃ שנים מהבהב (Yerushalmi ib. V, 9ᶜ bottom of page מעמעם) if asked a second time, he must not consent &c.

Nithpaël - נִתְהַבְהֵב to be affected by flames. Yoma 41ᵇ נ׳ הלשון if the band caught fire.

קָפַל I (see כָּפַל)
1) to double, fold, roll up. Yerushalmi Beitzah II, 61ᶜ bottom of page סדיני‌ן … היו קוֹפְלִין אותן they spread sheets on the floor, and, when the guests left, they folded them up. Menachot VI, 4 (75ᵇ), see כָּפַל. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 52 היה קוֹפֵל את הוילון וכ׳ he had the curtain rolled up and spoke to him; ib. section (Parashah) 74 מְקַפֵּל. Esther Rabbah to I, 5. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 52 שלשה … קְפָלוּהוּ for three months they kept the Tabernacle rolled up (did not put it up); Yalkut ib. 417; (Midrash Tanḥuma P’ḳudé 11 היה מונה ומפורק). Chullin 91ᵇ קְפָלָהּ הקב"ה לכל וכ׳ (Manuscript Hamburg קִיפֵּל) the Lord rolled up the entire land of Israel and placed it under him (Jacob); Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 69 קפלה כפינקס he folded it together like a book of writing tablets; and from—Transferred to overlap, combine. Midrash Tanḥuma Lekh 11 תשע … הקב"ה וכ׳ the Lord combined 980 generations in order to give the law of circumcision to Abraham (alluding to Psalms CV, 8); ib. תתקע"ד דור וכ׳ the Lord combined 974 generations in order to give the Law to the generation of the wilderness; Shir HaShirim Rabbah to IV, 4 (reference. to אלף המגן, ib.) אלף דור קָפַלְתִּי וכ׳ I combined a thousand generations and brought that shield (the Law) which was the desire of your heart. Bava Batra 121ᵇ שבעה קָפְלוּ וכ׳ (Rashb. קִיפְּלוּ) seven persons overlapped an entire world (lived through many generations): Methusalem saw Adam, Shem saw Methuselah &c.—Part. pass. קָפוּל; plural קְפוּלִים. Oholot XI, 3 ק׳ זו ע"ג זו folded up (packed) one above the other.

Piël - קִיפֵּל same. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 52 לנביאי או"ה אינו מְקַפֵּל אותו וכ׳ for the gentile prophets the Lord does not lift the curtain, but speaks to them from behind it. Shabbat II, 3 פתילת … שקִיפְּלָהּ וכ׳ a wick made of rags which one has twisted but not yet singed. Ib. XV, 3 מְקַפְּלִין את הכלים וכ׳ you may fold garments &c. Parah II, 3, see מוֹסֵרָה. Sotah 36ᵃ וקִיפְּלוּ את האבנים and they doubled up (packed) the stones, see infra; (Tosefta ib. VIII, 8 ונטלו); and from—Part. pass. מְקוּפָּל; f. מְקוּפֶּלֶת; plural מְקוּפָּלִים, מְקוּפָּלִין; מְקוּפָּלוֹת. Shabbat 58ᵃ; 147ᵃ היוצא בטלית מק׳ וכ׳ he that goes out with a cloak rolled up and laid over his shoulder. Ib. סוחרי כסות … מק׳ וכ׳ dealers in clothes who go out with cloaks rolled up and laid &c. Sifré Bamidbar 84 וכשהם חונין … מק׳ ועומד and when they encamped, the pillar of cloud remained rolled up. Taanit 31ᵃ אפי׳ מק׳ וכ׳ even when folded and lying in the chest; and e.—Nedarim VIII, 4, see infra.

Hifil - הִקְפִּיל to double up, lay up in layers, pack. Nedarim VIII, 4 (61ᵇ) עד שיַקְפִּילוּ המקצועות Bavli ed. (Yerushalmi ed. שיכפילו; Mishnah שיְקַפְּלוּ), see מַקְצוּעָה; (ib. 61ᵇ Gemarah שיכפלו, שיכפילו); Tosefta Demai I, 3 משיקפלו; Yerushalmi ib. I, beginning 21ᶜ משיקפלו.

Hof. - הוּקְפָּל to be laid up in layers, be folded up. Nedarim 62ᵃ הוּקְפְּלוּ רוב וכ׳ if most of the figs have been packed (most of the knives have been folded up).

comments.en: Some make the mistake of thinking that in order to fulfill the mitzva of simḥa on the festival they must buy the most expensive food and clothing available, just like rich people do, even though this is entirely beyond their means. In fact, the mitzva is for each person to spend in accordance with his means. One who has an average salary should buy meat and wine and other tasty foods in the way that people of average means prepare for an important meal. The simḥa of the meal depends on drinking wine and having more tasty foods than one’s normal weekday menu. It does not depend on how it compares with the meals of the wealthy. (See Peninei Halakha: Shabbat 2:3.)
comments.he: ויש טועים וסוברים שכדי לקיים את מצוות השמחה בחג, הם צריכים לקנות את המאכלים והבגדים היקרים ביותר, כדרך העשירים, מעל ומעבר ליכולתם. אבל המצווה היא שכל אדם יוציא עבור צורכי החג כפי הכנסתו. כלומר, מי שמשכורתו בינונית יקנה יין ובשר ושאר מטעמים כדרך שהבינוניים קונים לסעודה חשובה. שכן שמחת הסעודה תלויה בשתיית היין והוספת מטעמים מעבר למה שרגילים בימות החול ולא בהשוואה לעשירים (עיין בפניני הלכה שבת ב, ג, ובהרחבות שם וכאן).

מדליקין בפתילה מחורכת, ולא בסמרטוטין ואע"פ מחורכין. כל אילו שאמרו אין מדליקין בשבת מדליקין בהן ביום טוב, חוץ משמן שריפה. מפני מה אמרו אין מדליקין בשמן שריפה ביום טוב, לפי שאין שורפין לא תרומות ולא קדשים ולא חמץ ביום טוב.

מדליקין בפתילה מחורכת [ולא בסמרטוטין ואף על פי שמחורכין] כל אלו שאמרו אין מדליקין בהן בשבת מדליקין בהן ביו"ט חוץ משמן שריפה מפני מה אמרו אין מדליקין בשמן שריפה ביום טוב לפי שאין שורפין לא [תרומות] ולא קדשים ולא חמץ ביום טוב.

comments.en: A person who is clean shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle on the tent and on all the vessels and people who were there, or on him who touched the bones or the person who was killed or died naturally or the grave.
comments.he: וְלָקַ֨ח אֵז֜וֹב וְטָבַ֣ל בַּמַּ֘יִם֮ אִ֣ישׁ טָהוֹר֒ וְהִזָּ֤ה עַל־הָאֹ֙הֶל֙ וְעַל־כׇּל־הַכֵּלִ֔ים וְעַל־הַנְּפָשׁ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָֽיוּ־שָׁ֑ם וְעַל־הַנֹּגֵ֗עַ בַּעֶ֙צֶם֙ א֣וֹ בֶֽחָלָ֔ל א֥וֹ בַמֵּ֖ת א֥וֹ בַקָּֽבֶר׃

sections.en: Of all substances that emerge from the tree, one may light only with flax on Shabbat (Tosafot) because the other substances do not burn well. And of all substances that emerge from the tree, the only substance that becomes ritually impure with impurity transmitted by tents over a corpse is flax. If there is a dead body inside a house or a tent that is made from any materials that originate from a tree, everything in the house becomes ritually impure. However, only in the case of flax does the tent itself become impure. The wick of a garment, i.e., cloth made into a wick for a lamp, that one folded it into a size and shape suitable for a wick, but did not yet singe it slightly in order to facilitate its lighting, Rabbi Eliezer says: This wick is ritually impure. With regard to the laws of ritual impurity, it can, like other garments, still become ritually impure and one may not light with it on Shabbat. Rabbi Akiva says: It is ritually pure and one may even light with it on Shabbat.
sections.he: כָּל הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הָעֵץ אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בּוֹ אֶלָּא פִשְׁתָּן. וְכָל הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הָעֵץ אֵינוֹ מִטַּמֵּא טֻמְאַת אֹהָלִים אֶלָּא פִשְׁתָּן. פְּתִילַת הַבֶּגֶד שֶׁקִּפְּלָהּ וְלֹא הִבְהֲבָהּ, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, טְמֵאָה, וְאֵין מַדְלִיקִין בָּהּ. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, טְהוֹרָה, וּמַדְלִיקִין בָּהּ:

en:
נָתַר I (Biblical Hebrew; compare נתק) to sever, loosen.

Nifal - נִיתַּר, נִיתּוֹר
1) to be torn loose, be released. Yerushalmi Taanit II, 65ᵈ top, see נָטַשׁ II and נָתשׁ.—Transferred to be untied, released from an obligation; to become permitted. Shabbat II, 4 בשביל שתהא שׁוֹאֶבֶת in order that it (the wick) be soaked. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 14 בשעה … ושואבת וכ׳ while man is asleep, the soul rises and imbibes life for him from above. The above conclusion was that Rabbi Yehuda distinguishes between prohibitions involving substances from which people regularly separate themselves and prohibitions involving substances from which people are not used to keeping their distance. The Gemara asks: And anywhere that one does not distance himself from a prohibition, does Rabbi Yehuda issue a decree that one must keep away from a prohibited item to avoid accidentally using it?

But didn’t we learn in a mishna: A person may not pierce a hole in an eggshell, and fill it with oil, and place it beside a lamp so that the egg will drip additional oil into the lamp and thereby extend the time that it burns? And this is the ruling even if it is not an actual egg but an earthenware tube, from which most people consider it unsuitable to drink. The concern is lest one forget and take the tube and use the oil for some other purpose, and violate the prohibition against extinguishing a flame on Shabbat.

And Rabbi Yehuda permits using a tube in that manner, as he is not concerned lest one remove it. Apparently, Rabbi Yehuda does not issue a decree even with regard to an item from which people do not distance themselves, e.g., oil. The Gemara answers: There, due to the stringency of Shabbat, one distances himself, as on Shabbat one is careful to distance himself from a candle or anything placed alongside it.

And the Gemara raised a contradiction between this halakha of Shabbat and another halakha of Shabbat, as it was taught in a baraita: With regard to the rope of a bucket that was severed on Shabbat, where one needs the rope to draw water from a well, he may not tie it with a regular knot, as by Torah law it is prohibited to tie a permanent knot. Rather, he may tie it into a bow. However, Rabbi Yehuda says: One may wrap a money belt [punda] around it or a sash [pesikya], provided that he does not tie it into a bow, lest he tie a proper knot.

This presents a difficulty, as there is a contradiction between one statement of Rabbi Yehuda, who permits placing a tube of oil beside the lamp, and the other statement of Rabbi Yehuda, who prohibits tying a bow to reattach the severed rope of a bucket. There is likewise a difficulty between one statement of the Rabbis, who prohibit placing a tube of oil beside the lamp, and the other ruling of the Rabbis, where they permit tying a bow to reattach the severed rope of a bucket.

The Gemara answers: The apparent contradiction between one statement of the Rabbis and the other statement of the Rabbis is not difficult, as one usage of oil might be confused with another usage of oil. Given that it is permitted to use oil for other purposes, one is apt to utilize this oil as well. However, tying a bow will not be confused with the dissimilar tying of a knot. Consequently, the Rabbis do not issue a decree in that case.

The Gemara continues: Likewise, the contradiction between one statement of Rabbi Yehuda and the other statement of Rabbi Yehuda is not difficult, as the reason for the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda is not because he issues a decree to prohibit tying a bow due to the prohibition against tying a knot. Rather, the reason is more fundamental, because Rabbi Yehuda maintains that a bow itself is a full-fledged knot. According to Rabbi Yehuda, tying a bow is included in the prohibition against tying a knot on Shabbat.

And the Gemara raised a contradiction between one statement of the Rabbis and another statement of the Rabbis, as we learned in a mishna: One may tie a bucket with a sash, to draw water from a well, but one may not do so with a rope, and Rabbi Yehuda permits the use of a rope. Before addressing the aforementioned contradiction, the Gemara asks: The mishna is referring to a rope of what kind? If you say it is referring to a standard rope, does Rabbi Yehuda permit tying a knot in this rope? It is a permanent knot, as in tying the rope to the bucket he certainly comes to negate any other use of the rope. He performs a primary category of prohibited labor by tying a permanent knot.

Rather, it is obvious that the mishna is speaking about a rope used in the work of a weaver [gardi]. The legal status of this rope differs from that of an ordinary rope, as the weaver will certainly not leave his rope attached to a bucket and thereby negate any other use. Consequently, this knot is a temporary one.

The Gemara asks: And did the Rabbis issue a decree prohibiting the rope of a weaver due to a standard rope but they did not issue a decree prohibiting a bow due to a knot? The Gemara explains: Yes, the Rabbis indeed issued a decree prohibiting the rope of a weaver, as one rope may be interchanged with another rope, leading one to mistakenly tie a knot with a different rope. However, a bow is not interchanged with a knot.
he: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דְּלָא בָּדֵיל מִינֵּיהּ, מִי גָּזַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
וְהָתְנַן: לֹא יִקּוֹב אָדָם שְׁפוֹפֶרֶת שֶׁל בֵּיצָה וִימַלְּאֶנָּה שֶׁמֶן וְיִתְּנֶנָּה בְּצַד הַנֵּר בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתְּהֵא מְנַטֶּפֶת, וַאֲפִילּוּ הִיא שֶׁל חֶרֶס.
וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר! הָתָם, מִשּׁוּם חוּמְרָא דְּשַׁבָּת מִבְדָּל בְּדִילִי.

וּרְמִי דְּשַׁבָּת אַשַּׁבָּת, דְּתַנְיָא: חֶבֶל דְּלִי שֶׁנִּפְסַק, לֹא יְהֵא קוֹשְׁרוֹ אֶלָּא עוֹנְבוֹ. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כּוֹרֵךְ עָלָיו פּוּנְדָּא אוֹ פָּסִקְיָא, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַעַנְבֶנּוּ.
קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן!
דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן לָא קַשְׁיָא: שֶׁמֶן בְּשֶׁמֶן — מִיחַלַּף, עֲנִיבָה בִּקְשִׁירָה — לָא מִיחַלַּף.
דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּגָזַר עֲנִיבָה אַטּוּ קְשִׁירָה, אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָסָבַר עֲנִיבָה גּוּפַהּ קְשִׁירָה הִיא.

וְרָמֵי רַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן, דִּתְנַן: קוֹשְׁרִין דְּלִי בְּפָסִקְיָא אֲבָל לֹא בְּחֶבֶל, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר. חֶבֶל דְּמַאי? אִילֵּימָא חֶבֶל דְּעָלְמָא, ״וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר״? קֶשֶׁר שֶׁל קַיָּימָא הוּא, דְּוַדַּאי אָתֵי לְבַטּוֹלֵי!
אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא דְּגַרְדִּי.
וּגְזַרוּ רַבָּנַן חֶבֶל דְּגַרְדִּי אַטּוּ חֶבֶל דְּעָלְמָא? אִין, חֶבֶל בְּחֶבֶל — מִיחַלַּף, עֲנִיבָה בִּקְשִׁירָה — לָא מִיחַלְּפָא.

comments.en: Therefore, everything which the Sages instructed us to do in preparation for Shabbat must be done for Yom Tov as well. This includes washing one’s clothes in anticipation of the festival (Peninei Halakha: Shabbat 2:4; below 11:11), as well as taking a hot shower. It is also a mitzva for one who needs to get a haircut, shave, or cut his nails to do so (ibid. 2:5; below 11:9-10). Cleaning and straightening up the house before Yom Tov is also a mitzva, and men should participate in these preparations, as was the custom of great rabbis (ibid. 2:5-6).
comments.he: לפיכך, כל מה שאמרו חכמים שצריך לעשות לקראת שבת צריך לעשות לקראת החג, ובכלל זה מצווה לכבס את הבגדים לקראת החג (פניני הלכה שבת ב, ד; ולהלן יא, יא). וכן מצווה להתרחץ במים חמים לקראת החג. וכן מי שנצרך, מצווה שיסתפר ויתגלח ויגזוז את ציפורניו לקראת החג (פ"ה שבת ב, ה; להלן יא, ט-י). וכן מצווה לסדר את הבית ולנקותו לקראת החג, ומצווה להשתתף בהכנות הללו, כפי שנהגו גדולי הרבנים (פ"ה שבת ב, ה-ו).
אמ' ר' יהודה כשהיינו שרוין בעלית בית נתזה בלוד, היו נוקבין שפופרת של ביצה וממלאין אותה שמן ונותנין אותה על פי הנר בערב שבת עם חשיכה, כדי שיהא דולק ושוהא בלילי שבת, והיו שם זקנים ולא אמר אחד מהן דבר.
אם חברה בסיד ובגפסוס בערב שבת מותר.

א"ר יהודה כשהיינו שרויין בעליית בית נתזה בלוד היינו נוקבין שפופרת של ביצה וממלאין אותה שמן ונותנין אותה על הנר בע"ש עם חשיכה שיהא שוהה ודולק בלילי שבת [היו שם זקנים ולא אמר אחד מהן] דבר אם חברה בסיד ובגפסיס בע"ש מותר.

sections.en: The fundamental dispute in this mishna is with regard to the determination whether or not indirect acts of kindling and extinguishing fall within the parameters of the prohibition on Shabbat. The Rabbis said: A person may not pierce a hole in an eggshell and fill it with oil, and place it over the mouth of a lamp so that the egg will drip additional oil into the lamp and thereby extend the time that it burns. And this is the ruling even if it is not an actual egg but an earthenware vessel. And Rabbi Yehuda permits doing so. However, if the craftsman, who crafts ceramic vessels, attached the egg to the lamp from the outset, one is permitted to fill it with oil because it constitutes a single, large vessel. The Rabbis decreed that a person may not fill a bowl with oil, and place it beside the lamp, and place the unlit head of the wick into the bowl so that it draws additional oil from the bowl and thereby extend the time that the lamp burns. And Rabbi Yehuda permits doing so.
sections.he: לֹא יִקֹּב אָדָם שְׁפוֹפֶרֶת שֶׁל בֵּיצָה וִימַלְאֶנָּה שֶׁמֶן וְיִתְּנֶנָּה עַל פִּי הַנֵּר בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתְּהֵא מְנַטֶּפֶת, אֲפִלּוּ הִיא שֶׁל חֶרֶס. וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר. אֲבָל אִם חִבְּרָהּ הַיּוֹצֵר מִתְּחִלָּה, מֻתָּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא כְלִי אֶחָד. לֹא יְמַלֵּא אָדָם אֶת הַקְּעָרָה שֶׁמֶן וְיִתְּנֶנָּה בְצַד הַנֵּר וְיִתֵּן רֹאשׁ הַפְּתִילָה בְתוֹכָהּ, בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתְּהֵא שׁוֹאֶבֶת. וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר:

en: פֶּחָם, פֶּיחָם m. (Biblical Hebrew; נָפַח or פּוּחַ) that which is used for kindling, charcoal. Shabbat II, 5 מפני שהוא עושה פ׳ because (by extinguishing the light) he makes kindling material, i.e. prepares the wick for easier lighting (see הִבְהֵב). Ib. 31ᵇ. Kohelet Rabbah to IX, 8 נפח לפֶחָמוֹ the smith (the charcoal-burner) turns to his coal. Ib. to VII, 1; Yalkut Joshua 35, see פּוּצָם; and from—plural פֶּחָמִין, פֶּי׳. Tosefta Ma'aser Sheni V, 13; Yerushalmi ib. V, beginning 55ᵈ, see פָּחַם. Tosefta Beitzah III, 14 אין עושין פ׳ וכ׳ you must not make charcoal (prepare kindling material) even for immediate use (on the Holy Day). Mikvaot IX, 2 לא יטבול … בפ׳ וכ׳ one must not immerse a kettle with remnants of coal in it (which had been put there to be extinguished in water), unless one washes it again, Maimonides; [oth. opinion: with the soot on it, but he must scrape it off]. Kohelet Rabbah to I, 8 לכו … האיש ועל אותה החמת … מלאה פ׳ go ye and pray for this man (me), and for this bag formerly filled with precious stones and pearls, and now with pieces of coal; and e.

פָּטַר (Biblical Hebrew)
1) to break through, open. Bekhoroth VIII, 1 (46ᵃ) (reference. to Shemot XIII, 2) עד שיִפְטְרוּ רחם מישראל (not שיפטרוה
) provided they open the womb when the mother is an Israelite (although she conceived before her conversion); ib. 47ᵃ.—2) to send off, discharge, dismiss. Ketubot XIII, 5, and from או כנוס או פְּטוֹר (the betrothed has a right to say) either marry or release (me by divorce). Gittin VI, 5 פִּטְרוּהָ … לא אמר כלום if one says to friends, ‘release her’ … he has said nothing (they are not authorized to write a letter of divorce, as it might mean, release her of her debts &c.); ib. 65ᵇ ר׳ נתן אומר פַּטְּרוּהָ דבריו קיימין פִּיטְרוּהָ לא אמר כלום R. N. says, if he said paṭṭ’ruha (Piël), his words stand (a divorce is meant), but if he says piṭruha (Kal) &c. Ib. ר׳ נתן דבבלאה … בין פיטרוה לפטרוה וכ׳ R. N. who is a Babylonian, draws a distinction between piṭruha and paṭṭ’ruha; our Tannai (in the Mishnah) being a Palestinian does not &c. Ib. VIII, 4. פּוֹטֵר … בגט ישן a man may divorce his wife with an old letter of divorce (having been closeted with her after he had written it); Tosefta ib. VIII (VI), 3 אינו פוטר וכ׳ he must not divorce with an old letter, in order that the letter of divorce may not date farther back than (the conception of) her child; and from

—3) to dismiss, give leave, let go. Sotah IX, 6 ופְטַרְנוּהוּ בלא מזון and we let him (the stranger) go without provision. Midrash Till. to Psalms XCI מי גדול הפּוֹטֵר או הנִפְטָר which is the superior of the two? he who gives leave, or he who takes leave? Ib. (reference. to Breishit XXXII, 27) הרי יעקב פוטר למלאך behold, Jacob gives leave to the angel; and from

—4) (law) to discharge, acquit; (ritual) to exempt from obligation, to declare free from punishment, eventually from sacrificial atonement, opposed חִיֵּיב. Eruvin 65ᵃ יכול אני לִפְטוֹר וכ׳ I can (by my plea) release from judgment the whole world (all Israelites) from the destruction of the Temple to the present time, for we read (Isaiah LI, 21), Hear now this, thou afflicted and drunken &c. (a drunken person is irresponsible); ib. מאי יכולני לפטור נמי מדין תפלה this ‘I can release’ means also from responsibility for neglect of prayer (the drunken not being permitted to pray). Sukkah 45ᵇ. Shabbat II, 5 ר׳ יוסי פוטר בכלן וכ׳ R. J. declares (him that did it) free from punishment or eventual sacrifice in all those cases, except &c. Keritot IV, 2 ר׳ יהושע פוטר R. J. absolves him from bringing a sin-offering, opposed מחייב חטאת. Sanhedrin V, 5 אם מצאו לו זכות פְּטָרוּהוּ if they found evidence in his favor, they (the court) acquitted him; and see from—Transferred to cause exemption; to cover, include. Berakhot VI, 5 ברך על היין … פ׳ את היין וכ׳ if he recited the blessing over wine before the meal, he has therewith exempted the wine offered after the meal (from an additional blessing). Ib. 7 מברך על העיקר ופוטר את הטפלה he says the blessing over the chief dish, and with this he covers that which goes with it (see טְפֵלָה). Yevamot I, 1 חמש … פּוֹטְרוֹת צרותיהן fifteen women (of various kinship with the yabam, by which he is prevented from marrying any of them) cover their rivals (making them free from dependence on the yabam for marriage or discharge); and from—Part. pass. פָּטוּר; f. פְּטוּרָה; plural פְּטוּרִים, פְּטוּרִין; פְּטוּרוֹת (is, are) exempt, free, opposed חַיָּיב. Peah I, 6 ופ׳ מן המעשרות וכ׳ and he need not give the tithes, until &c. Bava Metzia VIII, 1 פ׳ (subaudi מלשלם) he is free from indemnity. Ib. VII, 10 מתנה … להיות פ׳ משבועה may have an agreement to be eventually exempt from making oath; להיות פ׳ מלשלם to be exempt from responsibility. Kiddushin I, 7 כל מצות הבן על האב … ונשים פ׳ to all paternal duties men are bound, but women (mothers) are exempt from them. Yevamot I, 2 כשם שבתו פ׳ כך צרתה פ׳ as well as his (the yabam’s) daughter is exempt (from the law of levirate marriage, because the yabam cannot marry her), so her rival is exempt; and see from

Piël - פִּיטֵּר to dismiss; to divorce. Gittin 65ᵇ, see supra. Kiddushin 31ᵇ פַּטְּרוּנִי dismiss (escort) me; and e.

Nifal - נִפְטָר,

Hithpaël - הִתְפַטֵּר
1) to be exempted, freed. Bekhoroth II, 1 לא נִפְטְרוּ מבכור וכ׳ they (the Levites) have not been exempted from consecrating the firstborn of clean animals, but only from redeeming their firstborn sons and the firstborn of asses; and e.

—2) to be dismissed, take leave, depart. Yoma I, 5 נפטרו והלכו להם they took leave and went. Sotah IX, 5. Berakhot 64ᵃ הנ׳ מחבירו וכ׳ he who leaves his friend (after escorting him a distance) must not say, ‘go in peace’, but, ‘go to peace’; הנ׳ מן המת וכ׳ he who takes leave of the dead (after burial) &c. Ib. 31ᵃ; Eruvin 64ᵃ לא יִפָּטֵר אדם וכ׳ one must not leave a friend otherwise than with a word of tradition (on legal or religious subjects), by which he may remember him; and from—Esp. to depart this world, to die. Berakhot 17ᵃ גדל בשם טוב ונ׳ בשם טוב מן העולם who grew (lived) with a good name, and left the world with a good name. Temurah 16ᵃ בשעה שנ׳ משה רבינו לגן עדן when Moses our teacher was to depart for paradise. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 96; and from—Yalkut Kohelet 989 בשעה … מִתְפַּטְּרִים וכ׳ when the children are dismissed from school.

Hifil - הִפְטִיר
1) to discard; ה׳ בשפה to discard with the lip, to spurn. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 37 מחרקין … ומַפְטִירִים בשפתותיהם gnashed their teeth … and spurned with their lips (reference. to Psalms XXII, 8). Masechet Der. Er. Chaldaic II מפְטִּירֵי שפה (= מפטירין בשפה).

—2) to dismiss, adjourn a meeting. Yerushalmi Berakhot IV, 7ᵈ top הַפְטֵר את העם dismiss the people (adjourn the meeting). Moʿed Katan 5ᵇ, see בָּכָה. Chullin 51ᵃ מַפְטִיר כנסיות one who dismisses the assemblies, janitor, see כְּנֶסֶת.—Pesachim X, 8, see אֶפִּיקוֹמָן; and e.

—3) [to recite before dismissal,] to conclude the reading from the Law by reading a portion of the Prophets, to read the Hafṭarah (see הַפְטָרָה). Megillah IV, 1 בשני … ואין מַפְטִירִין בנביא on Mondays, Thursdays and Saturday afternoons three persons read from the Law …, and we do not close with a lesson from the Prophets. Ib. 5 המפטיר בנביא הוא וכ׳ he who concludes with the prophetic lesson (being the last of those called up) has the privilege of &c., see פָּרַס; and from

פָּנִים common gender. plural (Biblical Hebrew; front, face; countenance, person. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Baḥod., p. 110ᵃ, and e. (פ׳ זעופות) פ׳ זועפות, see זָעַף. Mekhilta Beshalach, Vayassʿa, section (Parashah) 2; Yalkut Shemot 258, see חָשׁוּךְ. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 91 (reference. to Breishit XLI, 56) אין פְּנֵי הארץ אלא עשירים ‘the face of the land’ means the wealthy; בזמן שאדם עשיר יש לו פ׳ שמחים וכ׳ when a man is rich, he has a countenance which is glad to see his friend, but when he is poor אין לו פ׳ לראות וכ׳ he has not the face to see (his friend), because he is ashamed &c. Ketubot 7ᵇ והוא שבאו פ׳ חדשות provided a new face appears, i.e., a person that has not attended the wedding festivities before this. Ib. 8ᵃ אי איכא פ׳ חדשות if there is a new guest.—Bava Kamma 96ᵇ פ׳ חדשות באו לכאן things have assumed a new face, i.e. the object after its transmutation is no longer the same as the one stolen; and see from—נשא פ׳; גלה פ׳ &c., see נָשָׂא, גָּלָה &c.—Shir HaShirim Rabbah to VII, 9 מהדרין פ׳, see פָּנָה.—לחם הפ׳, see לֶחֶם.—Euphem. פ׳ של מטה, or פ׳ pudenda. Shabbat 41ᵃ. Berakhot 24ᵃ יכולה לכסות פָּנֶיהָ וכ׳ she can cover her nakedness &c. Niddah 14ᵇ; and from—Transferred aspect, manner, way of interpretation. Shir HaShirim Rabbah to II, 4 התורה שנדרשת מ"ט פ׳ טהור ומ"ט פ׳ טמא the Torah on the laws of which arguments are held, forty-nine in favor of ‘clean’ (permitted), and forty nine in favor of ‘unclean’ (forbidden); Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 2 תורה שהיא נדרשת מ"ט פ׳ the Torah which is interpreted in forty-nine ways; and from—לְפָ׳ a) for appearance sake, formally. Megillah 12ᵃ הם לא עשו אלא לפ׳ … אלא לפ׳ they (in bowing to the idol) acted merely for show (yielding to force), so the Lord dealt with them merely formally (not in full earnest, reference. to Eicha III, 33).—b) in front; (of time) before this, in the past. Chagigah II, 1 מה לפ׳ ומה לאחור what was before (creation), and what will be in the future (when the world will be no more; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 1 מה בי"ת זה סתום … ופתוח מִלְּפָנָיו וכ׳ as the letter ב (of בראשית, Breishit I, 1) is closed on all sides and open in front, so art thou not permitted to ask what is above and what is below, what was before and what will be hereafter; [oth. opinion מה לפ׳ ומה לאחור what is in the extreme east beyond the sphere, and what in the west; see, however, Rashi Haggai l. common gender. (Chagigah 11ᵇ), and Chagigah 16ᵃ].—Berakhot 5ᵇ לפני מטתי in front of my bed, explained סמוך למיטתי immediately after rising. Ib. 7ᵃ, and from יהי רצון מִלְּפָנֶיךָ (abbrev. יהר"מ may it be thy will. Ib. יהי רצון מִלְּפָנַי may it be my will. Ib. שלשה דברים בקש משה מִלִּפְנֵי וכ׳ for three things Moses prayed I before the Lord. Ib. I, 4 שתים לְפָנֶיהָ two benedictions preceding it (the reading of the Sh’mʿa); and see from—Sifra Vayikra, Ḥobah, Parah 13, Chaldaic XXIII אמש ושֶׁלְּפָנָיו ושֶׁלִּפְנֵי פנָיו yesterday and the day before yesterday, and the day before that.—לִפְנֵי עִוֵּר (also לפני only, see עִוֵּר I) the law prohibiting an act which may lead a person to sin (Vayikra XIX, 14). Pirkei Avot Zar. 14ᵃ וליחוש … אל׳ מפקדינן אל׳ דל׳ לא וכ׳ (Manuscript Munich אל׳ עור) but should we not apprehend, that he might sell (the incense) to others, who will burn it for idols? Said A., we are commanded to guard against an act directly leading to sin, but not against one that may indirectly cause sin; ib. 21ᵃ.—מִפְּנֵי for the sake of, on account of; מפני ש־ because. Shabbat II, 5 מ׳ שהוא מתיירא מ׳ גוים וכ׳ because he is afraid of invaders, of robbers, or of an evil wind. Berakhot I, 3 וסכנתי בעצמי מ׳ וכ׳, see סָכַן II. Ib. 3ᵃ מ׳ מה נכנסת וכ׳ why didst thou enter these ruins? Ib. מ׳ שלשה דברים for three reasons; מ׳ חשד because you give cause to suspicion; מ׳ המפולת because debris may fall on you; מ׳ המזיקין on account of demons; and see from—בִּפְנֵי in the presence of. Ib.ᵇ ב׳ המת in the presence of a dead person. Ib. 31ᵇ המורה הלכה ב׳ רבו he who gives a decision in his teacher’s presence; and see from—Kiddushin 64ᵇ הנודר עד פְּנֵי פסח וכ׳; Nedarim VIII, 2 הנודר עד לִפְנֵי הפסח וכ׳ if one says in his vow, ‘until p’né (lifné) Passover’, R. M. says, he is bound until Passover begins; R. J. says, until it is passed; Kiddushin 65ᵃ, see פְּנֵי I.

שְׁבִיל m. (Biblical Hebrew; שבל , Shaf. of יָבַל) path. Peah II, 1 ש׳ הרבים a public path through fields; ש׳ היחיד a private path, contradistinguished to דרך. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 25 ב"וד עושה לו ש׳ בדרך שמא … ש׳ בים a human being makes himself a path on trodden ground, can he make himself a path in the sea?; and from—plural שְׁבִילִים, שְׁבִילִין. Bava Kamma 81ᵃ ומהלכים בשְׁבִילֵי הרשות וכ׳ it is allowed to walk on private paths (through fields) until the second rainfall (see רְבִיעָה); Taanit 6ᵇ; Tosefta Sheviit VII, 18 ש׳ שבשדות. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 4 היו לפניו שני ש׳ וכ׳ if a person had before him two paths, one smooth &c. Yerushalmi Chagigah II, 77ᵃ bottom of page התורה הזו דומה לשני ש׳ וכ׳ the Torah is like two paths, the one of fire, the other of snow &c. Midrash Tanḥuma T’rumah 8 (reference. to Mishlei V, 6) שְׁבִילֶיהָ של תורה וכ׳ the paths of the Torah and its sections; and e.—Nazir 8ᵇ מנין שבילי שמיטה Variant (see Rashi) as many as the field paths in the Sabbatical year (ed. שבלי).—בִּשְׁבִיל on account of, for the sake of; because. Berakhot 58ᵃ בִּשְׁבִילִי for my sake. Ib. בש׳ אשתו ובניו for his wife and children. Taanit 20ᵃ בִּשְׁבִילְךָ for thy sake. Ib. 20ᵇ בִּשְׁבִילְכֶם for your sake. Shabbat II, 4 בש׳ שתהא מנטפת in order that it may drip. Ib. 5 בש׳ החולה שישן for the sake of a patient, that he may sleep. Sukkah 29ᵃ בש׳ ארבעה דברים for four reasons. Sotah 46ᵇ בש׳ שכנעני וכ׳ because this Canaanite showed the way with his finger. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 36 שלחה בש׳ וכ׳ she sent for R. J.; and see from

comments.he: עיר שהקיפוה נכרים או נהר וכן ספינה המיטרפת בים וכן יחיד שהיה נרדף מפני [נכרים ומפני לסטים] ומפני רוח רעה הרי אלו מחללין את השבת ומצילין את עצמן.

שתי חצירות אחת פתוחה לצפון ואחת לדרום וגגותיהן שוין [הגגות] רשות לעצמן והחצירות כל אחת ואחת רשות [לעצמה] היתה אחת מהן גבוהה עשרה טפחים ומיעטה באבנים ובכפתים ובסולם הצורי או שהביא נסר [שרחב] ארבעה טפחים [וקבעו] בה מערבין שנים אם רצו מערבין אחת פחות מכן מערבין שנים ואין מערבין אחד.
אין ממלין בעדשה בשבת. אם כחס על חבל, ועל משיחה, הרי זה מותר.

sections.en: One who extinguishes the lamp on Shabbat because he is afraid due to gentiles, from whom he is hiding in his home, and due to thieves, or if one is afraid due to an evil spirit, i.e., he is depressed and prefers sitting in the dark, or if he extinguished the flame due to the sick person so that he will sleep, he is exempt. However, in a case where he extinguishes the flame in order to spare the lamp, spare the oil, or spare the wick, he is liable. Rabbi Yosei exempts him in all of those cases, as in his opinion no labor prohibited by Torah law is being performed by extinguishing the flame, except for the case where he seeks to spare the wick. Only in that case is extinguishing a creative action because he makes the wick into charcoal by extinguishing the flame.
sections.he: הַמְכַבֶּה אֶת הַנֵּר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מִתְיָרֵא מִפְּנֵי גוֹיִם, מִפְּנֵי לִסְטִים, מִפְּנֵי רוּחַ רָעָה, וְאִם בִּשְׁבִיל הַחוֹלֶה שֶׁיִּישַׁן, פָּטוּר. כְּחָס עַל הַנֵּר, כְּחָס עַל הַשֶּׁמֶן, כְּחָס עַל הַפְּתִילָה, חַיָּב. וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי פּוֹטֵר בְּכֻלָּן חוּץ מִן הַפְּתִילָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא עוֹשָׂהּ פֶּחָם:

en: הַדְלָקָה f. (דלק) lighting, kindling. Shabbat 23ᵃ ה׳ עושה מצוה the kindling (of the Ḥanukhah lights) is the ceremony prescribed, contradistinguished to הנחה the placing it. Ib. II, 6 (31ᵇ) הַדְלָקַת הנר kindling the Sabbath lights. Yerushalmi Terumot V, 43ᶜ top למשחה לה׳ l’moshḥah (Bamidbar XVIII, 8) means (also) for lighting purposes (compare מִישְׁחָא). Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 15, beginning על הַדְלָקָתָן וכ׳ concerning feeding them with olive oil.

זָהִיר, זְהִירָה f. (זהר) looking out; strictly observant; careful, on one’s guard. Pirkei Avot II, 1 הוי ז׳ וכ׳ be as strict in the observance of minor religious duties &c. Ib. IV, 13; Bava Metzia 33ᵇ הוי ז׳ בתלמזד be careful in teaching the Law, see זָדוֹן. Sanhedrin 76ᵇ הוי ז׳ במי שיועצך וכ׳ Manuscript Munich (ed. מן היועצך, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note) beware of him who advises thee to his own advantage. Shabbat 23ᵇ הז׳ במזוזה he who is strict in the observance &c.; and from—plural זְהִירִין, f. זְהִירוֹת. Pirkei Avot II, 3 הוו ז׳ ברשות beware of the officials. Shabbat II, 6 על שאינן ז׳ וכ׳ because they are not careful in the observance of the laws concerning &c.; and from

זָקַק (Biblical Hebrew; compare זכך and דקק) [to make thin, fine, clear,]
1) to distil, smelt, see Piël צָרַף) to rivet, forge; to chain, to join; to bind, obligate.—Part. pass. זָקוּק, f. זְקוּקָה; plural זְקוּקִים, זְקוּקִין, f. זְקוּקוֹת, with ל chained to, connected with, dependent on. Menachot 27ᵃ העושין פירות יהיו ז׳ וכ׳ the fruit-bearing species of the festive wreath shall be combined with those which bear no fruits. Yerushalmi Berakhot VI, 10ᵃ bottom of page כשהיו כולן ז׳ וכ׳ when they were, all of them, dependent on one loaf (for saying grace). Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 43 כנגד שלש … זקוקות להן (not זקוקין) corresponding to the three laws for which, our Rabbis taught, women are made responsible (Shabbat II, 6). Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. II, 41ᵃ top ז׳ למלכות in constant intercourse with the government.—Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 9 לשנים היא זקוקה she is responsible to two (her husband and the Lord).—Shevuot VI, 3. נכסים … זוֹקְקִין וכ׳ movable chattel binds the immovable with reference to the obligation of making oath, i.e. the two claims preferred in one suit are considered as one lawsuit, and the oath must refer to both; Yerushalmi Ketubot XII, 36ᵃ bottom of page [read:] לזוֹקְקָן לשבועה to combine the two (as one lawsuit) with regard to the oath. Yevamot II, 5 זוֹקֵק את וכ׳ he holds his brother’s wife tied to the leviratical marriage, i.e. she cannot marry otherwise until released from him; and from V. זִיקָה.

Nifal - נִזְקַק (compare זָוַג Nithpaël)
1) to join, meet; to be engaged in. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 20 מעולם לא נ׳ וכ׳ the Lord never engaged in communication with woman. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 42; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 5; and e. נ׳ המלך וכ׳ the king was attached to, took an interest in the affairs of the country. Shabbat 12ᵇ אין מ"ה נִזְקָקִין לו the angels do not attend to his prayers.—[
2) (in a hostile sense) to attack. Breishit Rabbah l. common gender. באו ברברים לִיוָּקֵק לו (Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. l. common gender.; Ruth Rabbah introduction, and e. להִזְדַּוֵּוג) Barbarians came to attack him.]

—3) to live with; to be coupled. Ruth Rabbah to IV, 3 ע"מ שלא אֶזָּקֵק לה with the condition that I will not live with her. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 20 איני נִזְקֶקֶת וכ׳ I shall never again live with &c.—Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 15; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Haḥod., p. 43ᵇ שיהא אדם נִזְקָק לביתו in order that man be attached to his house (love his wife); Yalkut Psalms 738; and e.

Hifil - הִזְקִיק to oblige. Sukkah 28ᵃ הִזְקַקְתּוּנִי וכ׳ will you force me to say &c.?

Hof. - הוּזְקָק to be made dependent on, to obligate one’s self, to be obliged to regard. Bava Batra 170ᵃ אם הוּזְקָקוּ וכ׳ Manuscript Munich (ed. אם כתוב בו הוּזְקַקְנוּ) if they (the parties to the deed) bound themselves to depend on the signatures of witnesses, &c. (ed. if it was written in the document, we obligate ourselves &c.).

Nithpaël - נִזְדַּקֵּק
1) to be engaged in, to care. Midrash Tanḥuma Korah 6 לא נִזְדַּקְּקוּ להשיבו (Yalkut Bamidbar 750 נִזְקָקוּ) they did not care to answer him.

—2) to attach one’s self to, to make love to. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 9.

—3) (in an evil sense) to get at, to harm. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 5 בקש להִזְדּקֵּק להם wanted to harm them.

Piël - זִיקֵּק (Biblical Hebrew) to smelt, refine, distil. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 31 עד שמְזַקְּקוֹ until he has refined the gold.—Part. pass. מְזוּקָּק, f. מְזוּקֶּקֶת. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 14 התורה … ומז׳ וכ׳
the Torah is clarified and distilled in forty nine ways.—2) to chain, tie, connect.—Part. pass. as ab. Yerushalmi Chagigah III, beginning 78ᵈ במז׳ לקדש it treats of an object which is tied (has been made subject) to the law regulating sacred matter, i.e. treated as if it were sacred matter, see טָהֳרָה.

1) [rolled, rounded] cake.—plural חַלּוֹת. 'Uktzin III, 5 ח׳ חריע (Tosefta Ma'aser Sheni I, 13 חַלַּת (collect. noun), and e., see חֲרִיעַ.—Menachot III, 6 שתי ח׳ the two loaves (offered on the Feast of Weeks, Vayikra XXIII, 17).—Bava Batra V, 3; 'Uktzin III, 11 ח׳ דבש honey-combs; and from

—2) (with reference. to Bamidbar XV, 20, sq.) Ḥallah, the priest’s share of the dough. Shabbat II, 6, see זָהִיר. Hallah I, 1 חייבין בח׳ are subject to the law of Ḥallah.—Ib. II, 7 שעור הח׳ the quantity to be set aside for the priest. Ib. 8 מעיסה שלא הורמה חַלָּתָהּ Manuscript Munich (see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note) from a dough from which the priest’s share has not yet been taken; and from—plural as ab. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Shimu, p. 118ᵃ שתי ח׳ two portions (one for being burnt, and one for the priest); Yerushalmi Eruvin III, end, 21ᶜ; Shir HaShirim Rabbah to I 6; and e.—Transferred ḥallah, the sanctification of creation, man. (reference. to Mishlei XXIX, 4, ואיש תרומות) that is Adam שהיה גמר חַלָּתוֹ וכ׳ who was the final sanctification of the world; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 17, end.—Ḥallah, name of a treatise of the Mishnah, Tosefta and Talmud Yerushalmi, of the Order of Z’raïm.

Yerushalmi Berakhot II, 4ᵈ top אשרי … כשעת לֵידָתוֹ וכ׳ happy he whose time of death is like his time of birth, as when he was born he was innocent &c. Ib. 23ᵇ; and from—plural לֵידוֹת. Yerushalmi ib. III, 50ᶜ; and from

Shabbat II, 6 על שלש וכ׳ for three sins &c. Sanhedrin 20ᵃ, and from אמרו עָלָיו על וכ׳ they relate about &c. Niddah 23ᵇ מי שלבו דוה עליו whose heart within him &c., see דָּוָה; and see from—על יד, על ידי, see יָד; על מנת, see מְנָת, &c.—Pirkei Avot Zar. 30ᵃ, and e. עָלי ועל צוארי, see צַוָּאר.

comments.en: And ten upon the serpent: Its mouth was sealed shut. Its hands and feet were cut off. It eats dust. It sheds its skin and suffers like a woman in childbirth, and its voice carries from one end of the world to the other, yet its voice is not heard. "And I will put enmity..." (Genesis 3:15) Rabbi Chelfai said in the name of Rabbi Meir: Even if it eats delicacies and drinks the sweetest wine, it becomes dust in its mouth, as it says "and dust shall be the serpent's bread" (Isaiah 65:25). It gives birth every seven years. (Bechorot 8a) A person sees an animal or bird and is not bothered, but when he sees a snake he is bothered and curses it. Everything receives blessing but it remains accursed. Rabbi Meir would say a tradition: "And I will remove the evil beasts from the earth" (Leviticus 26:6) - this refers to the snake. And ten upon the earth: That it would absorb water on its own from now on: "And a mist rose up from the earth" (Genesis 2:6) That it is afflicted in its fruits. That it is afflicted with blight and mildew. That mountains and valleys were made upon it. That thornbushes and gravel were created upon it. That barren trees grew upon it. That thorns and thistles grew upon it. They plant a lot but it produces little. That it will testify about its dead in the future, as it says "And the land will reveal its blood, and will no longer cover its slain" (Isaiah 26:21). That it is destined to wear out like a garment, as it says "And the earth will wear out like a garment" (Isaiah 51:6). Why were these forty decrees? Corresponding to the 40 days that the fetus is formed. Another interpretation: Corresponding to these decrees, the Sages instituted 40 lashes in the court. How so? When a person stumbles in a sin that makes him liable for death by the hand of Heaven, they bring him to court and lash him, and immediately forgive him entirely. This is what is taught: "There are four death penalties by the court." (All those liable for excision who were lashed were exempted from their excision - Makkot 23a.) Rabbi Eliezer says: Adam was the blood of the world, and when Eve spilled it [by causing his death], she became liable for the blood of menstruation. Adam was the challah of the world, and when Eve defiled it [through sin], she became liable for separating challah. Adam was the light of the world, and when Eve extinguished it [through sin], she became liable to light the Shabbat candles. This corresponds to what was taught: "For three sins women die in childbirth: menstruation, challah, and lighting the candles" (Shabbat 31b).
comments.he: ועשרה על הנחש: א') נסתם פיו, ב') קצצו ידיו ורגליו, ג') אוכל עפר, ד') מפשיט עורו ומצטער כיולדה וקולו הולך מסוף העולם ועד סופו ואין קולו נשמע, ה') ואיבה אשית, ו') א״ר חלפאי בשם ר״מ אפילו אוכל פטומין ושותה כל מתוק נעשה עפר בפיו שנאמר (ישעיה ס״ה) ונחש עפר לחמו, ז') מוליד לשבע שנים, (בכורות ח' ע״א) ח') אדם רואה חיה ועוף ואינו מקפיד וכשרואה נחש מקפיד ומקללו, ט') הכל מתברך והוא בקלקולו, י') היה ר' מאיר אומר עליו בקבלה (ויקרא כ״ו) והשבתי חיה רעה מן הארץ.- ועשרה על הארץ: א') שהיתה שותה מים מאליה מכאן ואילך ואד יעלה מן הארץ, ב') שהיא לוקה בפירותיה, ג') שהיא לוקה בשדפון ובירקון, ד) שנעשו בה הרים ובקעות, ה') שנבראו בה טרשים וקשקשים (קש וגבבא), ו') שעלו בה אילני סרק, ז') שעלו בה חוחין ודרדרין, ח') שזורעין הרבה והיא עושה מעט, ט') שהיא עתידה להעיד על הרוגיה שנאמר (ישעיה כ״ו) וגלתה הארץ את דמיה ולא תכסה עוד על הרוגיה, י') שהיא עתידה לבלות כשמלה שנאמר (שם נ״א) והארץ כבגד תבלה. ומפני מה ארבעים גזרות הללו? כנגד מ' יום שהולד נוצר בו, ד״א כנגד גזרות הללו קבעו חכמים בב״ד מלקות ארבעים. הא כיצד אדם נכשל בעבירה נתחייב בה מיתה בידי שמים מביאין אותו בב״ד ומלקין אותו ומיד מוחלין כולו וזהו ששנינו ד' מתות ב״ד. (כל חייבי כריתות שלקו נפטרו מידי כריתתן (מכות כ״ג ע״א) ר״א אומר אדם הראשון דמו של עולם וכששפכתו אשתו נתחייבה בדם נדה. אדם הראשון חלתו של עולם היה וכשטמאתו אשתו נתחייבה בהפרשת חלה, אדה״ר נרו של עולם וכיון שכיבתו אשתו נתחייבה בהדלקת נר שבת, ההוא דשנינו על שלש עבירות נשים מתות בשעת לידתן בנדה בחלה ובהדלקת הנר (שבת ל״א ע"ב).

sections.en: This mishna concludes the aggadic treatment of the topic of kindling the Shabbat lights. For three transgressions women are punished and die during childbirth: For the fact that they are not careful in observing the laws of a menstruating woman, and in separating ḥalla from the dough, and in lighting the Shabbat lamp.

וַדַּאי, וַודַּי, וַדָּאִית, וַדָּיָיה, (יַדָּאָה) f. (ידע)

Berakhot 33ᵇ הַוַּ׳ (see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note) Thou, the known one!—Arakhin I, 1 זכר ו׳ a person distinctly male, נקבה ודאית distinctly female (no hermaphrodite &c.). Yoma VIII, 8, and from אשם ו׳, see אָשָׁם.—Shabbat II, 7 הו׳ that which undoubtedly requires the separation of the tithes, opposed דְּמַאי.—Yerushalmi Beitzah I, 60ᵇ וַודָּייוֹ, וַודָּיָיהּ where there is no doubt about it, opposed ספיקו, ספיקה. Kiddushin IV, 3 (74ᵃ) וַדָּאָן the sure cases among them.—Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 2, end אכילה וודייה Arukh ed. Kohelet (ed. ידאית) the eating (in Shemot XXIV, 11) was a real one (physical refreshment, no metaphor); and see from

—2) (gramm.) emphatic form by means of He paragogic. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 3 לכה וודאית וכ׳ (strike out the gloss הה"א בסוף וכ׳) the word l’khah (Shemot III, 3) is emphatic (as if = לְךָ unto thee it belongs), if not thou &c.; Yerushalmi Sukkah IV, 54ᶜ top לך יודייה (read: לכה וו׳) the l’khah (Psalms LXXX, 3) has the emphatic form (unto thee
as well as unto us).—3) (noun) certainty, undisputed fact.—אין ספק מוציא מידי ו׳ doubt cannot take a case out of the status of certainty. Pirkei Avot Zar. 41ᵇ הוי ספק וּוַ׳ ואין וכ׳ here is a doubt (the idolatrous character of an object may have been given up) against a certainty (that it was an idol) and the doubt cannot set aside the certainty. Pesachim 9ᵃ; and from—בְּוַ׳, וַ׳ (adverb) surely, indeed; in reality. Yerushalmi Ketubot V, 29ᵈ. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 98 עלית בו׳ ‘thou didst ascend’ thy father’s couch (Breishit XLIX, 4) means in reality (no metaphor). Ib. חללת ו׳ ‘thou didst defile’ (ib.) is to be taken literally. Pesachim l. common gender. דו׳ מעשרי for it is sure that they separate the tithes. IV, 1; and from—Makhshirin I, 6 הטומן פירותיו וכ׳ if one hides his fruits in water against thieves.—Kohelet Rabbah to X, 8 שהוא ט׳ וכ׳ that he buried it there; and e.—Part. pass. טָמוּן. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 3 ויִטָּמְנוּ ד"ת בפיך and the words of the Law shall be stored up in thy mouth. 1) to hide, keep. Bava Kamma 61ᵇ שדרכם להַטְמִין וכ׳ which it is customary to hide in the stack. Bava Metzia 61ᵇ לא יַטְמִין … במלח he must not keep his weights in salt (by which they gain in weight); and from—Part. pass. מוּטְמָן, see supra.

Berakhot 7ᵃ ותתנהג עם בניך וכ׳ and deal with thy children mercifully. Sanhedrin 23ᵃ מי חותם עִמָּהֶן who is to sign as witness with them; and from

1) sunset, evening. Berakhot I, 3, sq. בָּעֶ׳ in the evening (at prayer); and see from—Transferred decline. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 50 בָּעֶרֶב בָּא עַרְבָהּ של סדום baʿereb (Breishit XIX, 1), the evening of Sodom has come. Esther Rabbah introduction מי יתן ערבה, see בֹּקֶר; and from

—2) entrance, the day preceding a certain day, the year preceding a certain period, eve. Shabbat II, 7 ע׳ שבת (abbrev. ע"ש) on Friday. Pesachim 99ᵇ ע׳ הפסח the eve of the Passover. Taanit IV, 7 ע׳ תשעה באב the day preceding the ninth of Pirkei Avot Sheviit I, 1 ע׳ שביעית the year preceding the Sabbatical year; and see from—Dual עַרְבַּיִם. עָשַׂר , Piël עִשֵּׂר (Biblical Hebrew;
1) to give one-tenth, separate tithes. Shabbat 119ᵃ עַשִּׁר וכ׳, see עָשַׁר. Ma'asrot IV, 2 ושכחו לעַשְּׂרָן but had forgotten to pay the tithe of them.
